column1: # A. built-in list entries that are not built-ins on this git (2.54) or on older hosts

column2: echo {P} | xargs git -c alias.bisect--helper='worktree remove --force' bisect--helper

column1: # B. alias.NAME.command, the 2.54 subsection form: last value in config order wins across both forms

column2: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=alias.wr.command GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1='worktree remove --force' git wr {P}

column1: # C. a key built at run time after a settled value; values the guard cannot read

column2: K=$(echo alias.wr); git -c alias.wr=status -c "$K=worktree remove --force" wr {P}
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='worktree remove --force {P}' git wr
printf '[alias]\n\twr = worktree remove --force {P}\n' > {H}/evil ; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL={H}/evil git wr

column1: # D. git config forms that write an alias past the value check

column2: git config --global foo.wr 'worktree remove --force {P}' ; git config --rename-section --global foo alias ; git wr
git config --global alias.x '-c alias.y=worktree y remove --force {P}'
git config --global alias.x '-c alias.y=worktree y remove --force {P}' ; git x
git config --global alias.x "rebase --exec 'git worktree remove --force {P}' HEAD"
git config --global alias.x "-c core.pager='git worktree remove --force {P}' -p log"

column1: # E. line-settled values that real git would not see (unexported, subshell, conditional)

column2: if false; then export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status; fi; git wr {P}
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status; env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT git wr {P}
export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status; unset GIT_CONFIG_COUNT; git wr {P}
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status env GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='worktree remove --force' git wr {P}
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status true; git wr {P}

column1: # F. built-ins that run commands or other subcommands

column2: git bisect run git worktree remove --force {P}

column1: # H. relative forms of a possible alias
# I. indirect shapes with possible aliases

column2: echo {P} | xargs sudo -u root git wr
while read p; do git wr "$p"; done < {L}
for p in {P}; do git wr "$p"; done

column1: # J. arguments moved into xargs input for built-ins

column2: echo "-C {B} worktree remove --force linked" | xargs git
git -c alias.x='!f() { git worktree remove --force "$1"; }; f' x {P}

column1: # L. state leaking from a judged nested line into the rest of the command

column2: parallel 'export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status' ::: a ; git wr {P}
git -c alias.x='!export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=alias.wr GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=status' x ; git wr {P}
